rv.q: THE Neil Diamond MUSICAL: A BEAUTIFUL NOISE succeeds because it understands that distinction.

The show is fun and filled with energy as it brings the audience into his world, balanced with contemplative moments as Neil struggles with his depression and works through the issues that brought him to this place in life.
A BEAUTIFUL NOISE is a profound character study that shines a spotlight on the music industry and the challenges of navigating it.
I left thinking that of all the shows that have graced the stage of the Fox Arts Center this season, this is one that should not be overlooked or missed.
Fun and frolicking, A Beautiful Noise shines.

A BEAUTIFUL NOISE is a powerful testament to love, healing, the talent of a tormented man, and the women who, through their love, became his muses and guided him through the darkest times of his life.
Neil Diamond: A BEAUTIFUL NOISE made for an unexpectedly entrancing night at the theatre.
It’s a feel-good evening at the theatre that ends just the way it should—on a high note.

The stellar cast accommodates theater goers on both sides of the Diamond spectrum and by the end of the two-act musical the average music fan will be surprised by how many Diamond songs he or she knows by heart and how good some of those songs truly are.
His robust voice, impressive in its own right, wonderfully encapsulates Diamond’s iconic vocals.
That decision gives A Beautiful Noise surprising heft for a jukebox musical, as it puts its protagonist on the couch and invites the audience to a therapeutic singalong.
With impeccable performances and a thought provoking narrative, the First National Tour of A Beautiful Noise is well deserved of its praise.
This tour is aces from start to finish.
It’s a visual feast, a stunning sing-along, and an all-around excellent outing.
"A Beautiful Noise" is the latest example of a musical that succeeds not just on the strength of its pre-sold extremely well-known songs but because it is exceptionally well written and directed.
To say I was blown away is an understatement.
Fradiani’s performance is extraordinary, and his success is ultimately what makes this show so utterly enjoyable.
If you are a Neil Diamond fan it is hard not to love this show.
As the younger Diamond, "American Idol" winner Nick Fradiani sounds uncannily like Neil and brings rock-star presence to everything.
The exuberant concert scenes capture the razzle-dazzle of Diamond's stage shows and turn it into a fully interactive experience.
Despite the show’s somewhat dark subject matter, it’s a fascinating and unique story. The show is high energy, well-produced and glitzy, and it’s an enjoyable ride because the music is so memorable.
I enjoyed this juke-box musical more than I expected and learned much about Neil Diamond the man.
No one will accuse Anthony McCarten, who wrote the book, of subtlety with this script.
The fan in me didn’t mind all that and appreciated the chance to hear a deep and varied songbook performed with skill, energy and new orchestrations.
Neil Diamond fans will be entertained by the 30 hit songs in this production, however many are only partially sung due to time constraints.
What stands out leaving the theater is how much Diamond’s songs have been the aural wallpaper of so many of our lives.
From those Jersey Boys through the Temptations and now Neil Diamond, a lesson of incessant road touring over the decades is you may generate — and, who knows, even keep? — millions of dollars.
“A Beautiful Noise” reaches for all of those very things, but does so a bit timidly.

“A Beautiful Noise” captures the stadium-sized energy of a Diamond show with recreations of “Brother Love’s Traveling Show” and a medley of “Soolaimon,” “Thank the Lord For the Night Time” and “Crunchy Granola Suite” — the latter with some quick costume changes for Fradiani.
For that reason, while I wholeheartedly endorse it for any Neil Diamond fan or music lover of a certain age, I can’t really say it’s a good fit for kids.
The show stands out as one the stronger productions in the recent flurry of jukebox musicals, bio-musicals of artists and bands.

Despite the energetic ensemble’s best efforts, all momentum dissipates during the morose second act, and an off-key finale leaves audiences in a meh mood that is only moderated by the mandatory “Sweet Caroline” curtain call.
However — and there’s no way to beat around the bush — as a musical, A Beautiful Noise is not a success.

But “A Beautiful Noise” attempts to be more than just a concert, and in so doing, it creates the clunkiest framing device and the least likable protagonist possibly in the history of jukebox musicals.
Overall, “A Beautiful Noise” is not — to borrow from the “Sweet Caroline” fan chant — “so good, so good, so good,” but rather “so meh.”

cn.t: Critics find this jukebox musical delivers Neil Diamond's beloved hits with energy and strong performances, though opinions split on its therapy-framed narrative exploring his depression—some appreciate the unexpected depth, others find it uneven.
